subtitulo: A port warehouse turned into a trade school
texto: Warehouse number 3 on the Herrera quay has stood empty for twenty years: a concrete shed from 1962, with twelve-metre spans and a sawtooth roof that no longer covers anything. The proposal neither empties it nor rebuilds it. It repairs the roof, opens the floor at three points and inserts a timber building that never once touches the existing walls.

The workshops — carpentry, metal, boilermaking — occupy the ground floor, where the slab takes the heavy machinery and the quay doors let material in and out without detours. Above them, a tray of laminated timber holds the classrooms and a running corridor from which you can watch the work below. Learning a trade is, above all, watching someone who knows how to do it.

The works stop at the water's edge. The quay is left as it is, with its bollards and its rails, and all that is added is a ramp for launching whatever gets built inside. The building does not intend to reclaim the port: it intends to remain part of it.

subtitulo: Twelve houses and a public path above the estuary
texto: Olabeaga is a long street propped against the hillside, with houses on one side only and the estuary on the other. The site is the gap left by a demolished workshop: fifteen metres of frontage, thirty of depth and seven metres of level difference between the street and the path above.

Instead of a block, twelve terraced houses stepping down with the slope. Each has two fronts — the estuary to the south, the hillside to the north — and a strip of services in between that absorbs the level change in two steps. Every dwelling has the same plan and differs only in the level it sits on.

The path linking the twelve houses runs at mid-height, between the street and the upper track, and works as a shortcut for the neighbourhood: you can walk up it without knocking on any door. It is the only part of the project that belongs to nobody in particular.

subtitulo: A neighbourhood facility inside a block in Sants
texto: The inside of the block is taken up by single-storey sheds that are no longer used and by a three-metre wall separating them from the housing. The brief asked for a neighbourhood facility; the project begins by deciding which part of the wall stays and which part comes down.

Two whole sheds are kept, along with the row of columns of a third. Between them a long courtyard appears, running east to west, distributing access to the three pieces of the programme: the multipurpose hall, the workshops and the senior citizens' centre. The rest is shade: a pergola of reclaimed beams that covers the courtyard without ever enclosing it.

The construction is deliberately poor: fair-faced brickwork, off-the-shelf aluminium windows and sheet metal over the old sheds. The budget concentrates on the ground, the water and the trees, which is what the neighbourhood will actually use.
